More lava inside the caldera. Round 1's floor was a pale ash plain round one lake. Round 2 adds four kinds of lava, all in world.mjs so every page agrees.

A bigger lava lake. 10.5 ha, up from 6.6. It now reaches further south, toward the terraces, and further east, where the northern flow and the crust fields meet it. The 8th's cape and the 9th's shore and bridge are where they were: the lake grew away from the fairways.

Two lava rivers across the floor. The Spill rises from a vent below the terraces and runs across the floor below the terraces, well right of the 6th and the 7th, into the lake's south shore. The northern flow comes from a vent far across the floor into the lake's east end. Both run in channels between their own levees, like the 1st's river. Neither crosses a line of play.

Glowing crust fields. Six lobes of fresh black lava, crusted over and glowing at the seams, laid along the flows (15 ha in all): native ground, a little raised, a bad lie but not a penalty. They fill the far floor seen from the 5th tee and line the rivers.

Lava below the terraces. A pool of lava at the foot of the 6th's basalt columns, just right of the straight line from the tee to the green: a drive at the green that leaks right finds it. The pool under the lavafall stays.

Geysers outside. A small geyser field on a white sinter terrace in the barranco's floor, 115 m right of the 2nd's line at the drive. The biggest one erupts every few minutes; the other two steam. Scenery only, out of play.
A wider lava river on the 1st. 22 m across (from 15), with higher levees. It now comes within about 45 m of the line at the bend, so a big slice finds it; at the drive it is still 60–75 m right.
Kept as it was, by request: the 9th's climb onto the island, and every hole's routing, greens, bunkers and tees. All the shape checks pass as before (the overview's tips column is unchanged).
Still open: the faint far west wall over the Notch from the 4th tee; the stray straight scarp near the 1st's forest; no emitter to the engine format yet.
